o1.biggest_strength: It turns the old pause test back on and gives the product team clear, reason-by-reason screen copy they could build quickly.
o1.biggest_mistake: It keeps a 50% discount for people switching apps without evidence that this group is worth discounting, and the value of that discounted save is not cleanly counted.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove or test the switching-app discount, tighten the revenue math around discounted months, and make the launch priority and measurement plan sharper.

o2.biggest_strength: It names the critical dependency plainly: the pause does almost all the work, so rebuilding it is the first sprint priority and the flow should not launch without it.
o2.biggest_mistake: It misses the softer reactivation option for the trip-over group and slightly overstates the reminder save by treating all 'not making progress' cancellers as equally suited to a reminder.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the optional trip reminder, split the progress group by reminder status in the forecast, and show the 12-month value calculation more transparently.

reason: Output 2 is the one I would hand to the team because it is more disciplined about not discounting people who will come back anyway, puts the pause rebuild first, and gives a clearer launch risk and measurement plan. Output 1 is strong, but the unsupported switching-app discount and fuzzier revenue treatment make it less owner-safe.
